header: Date: 2027-07-18 | Time: 15:00-15:45 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Eli Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Arjun Patel (Caspian CTO), Sofia Ruiz (ML Lead), Liam O'Connor (SRE)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual medical document understanding and tool-calling. Customer evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for PHI-sensitive pipelines. Key tradeoffs: context length (8k->32k->64k), latency vs cost, multilingual quality, support for function/tool calling and streaming. Agreed to run benchmarks and share security artifacts.
topics: Open model comparisons (Llama-3 8k/32k, Mistral, open-instruct variants)
Context length needs (8k vs 32k vs 64k) and partitioning long docs
Multilingual quality and tokenization for Spanish / Portuguese / Mandarin
Tool-calling / function calling for retrieval + structured responses
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) security/latency/cost tradeoffs
Quantization and perf (int8, q4_k, q2) and KV cache behavior
transcript:
[00:00] Eli Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give a quick intro and then jump into model selection needs. Maya and I from Redwood.
[00:12] Dr. Arjun Patel: Thanks, Eli. We're excited; short intro — we're building an assistant to summarize multi-page medical notes and do structured extraction for downstream billing workflows. PHI sensitive, so network controls important.
[00:27] Maya Kapoor: Great, are you leaning hosted, Dedicated, or fully private VPC?
[00:34] Sofia Ruiz: Right now we prefer Hosted for dev but for prod we need either Dedicated pools with isolation or Private VPC. Our compliance team will push for private if we can't get clear KMS + audit.
[00:47] Liam O'Connor: Also curious about context length — notes can be 20k+ tokens after OCR, is there advice on chunking vs 64k contexts?
[00:57] Eli Chen: Yeah so quick overview: open models tradeoff — Llama-3-family gives good instruct performance, Mistral variants strong for short-ish instructions. Redwood supports long-context variants (32k/64k), and we do automatic prefix caching and KV cache to avoid re-computation on repeated prompts.
[01:18] Dr. Arjun Patel: When you say KV cache, is that per-session in memory on the GPU or persisted? sometimes we need to resume sessions across restarts.
[01:27] Maya Kapoor: Good question — KV is kept in-memory on the inference node for active sessions; we have strategies to persist or warm caches for dedicated/private deployments. For Hosted, we do transient caches and recommend an external state store if you need persistence.
[01:41] Sofia Ruiz: Curious about tokenization — for Spanish/Portuguese we saw degraded quality with a small-vocab tokenizer on some models. Any guidance?
[01:49] Eli Chen: Tokenization differences are model-dependent; Llama-3 32k performs well across latin-based languages, but we encourage running a quick eval on your sample docs. Maya: we ran the initial multilingual eval last quarter and saw Mistral-instruct drop off on Mandarin.
[02:04] Maya Kapoor: Right. Also note that quantization can affect multilingual fidelity — aggressive q2/q3 sometimes hurts non-English. If you want, we can run a quantized vs fp16 comparison on your data.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: For tool-calling, we need function calling to trigger a retrieval microservice and return structured JSON back to our pipeline. Does Redwood support function or tool calling?
[02:28] Eli Chen: Yes, we support function/tool calling and structured output hooks. We have examples for retrieval augmented generation where the model calls out to your retrieval API, and we can stream structured chunks back. We also support function signatures like OpenAI-style function calling.
[02:44] Dr. Arjun Patel: How about latency implications when using long context and tool calls — we'd like sub-800ms 95th p99 for short queries but can tolerate higher for long-doc summarize.
[02:53] Maya Kapoor: Latency depends a lot on model size and quantization. For example, a 32k Llama-3 quantized to int8 on Dedicated can hit 150-300ms per token in many cases; for short queries you're looking at network roundtrip + model time so 800ms p95 is achievable with Dedicated low-latency pools. Hosted can be similar but depends on tenancy and warm vs cold.
[03:14] Sofia Ruiz: Do you provide throughput/latency profiles per model?
[03:18] Eli Chen: Yes, we have Redwood-verified performance profiles — we'll share the bench spreadsheet. We'll include 8k/32k/64k config runs, and quantized variants.
[03:29] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:34] Sofia Ruiz: On security, our legal team needs SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration and logs for audit.
[03:42] Eli Chen: We provide SOC2 reports, SAML SSO, RBAC, and integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private/Dedicated. For Hosted we offer managed KMS with encrypted-at-rest keys, and we can sign an addendum for data residency where needed.
[03:59] Liam O'Connor: Any details on network egress rules for Private VPC? We need specific CIDR whitelist and no public internet from the inference nodes.
[04:07] Maya Kapoor: For Private, you control the VPC; our control plane talks over a customer-managed peering or private link. We can support zero-egress patterns; we'll need your network team to confirm routing.
[04:18] Dr. Arjun Patel: About model hallucination — we need structured extraction with high precision. Does Redwood support calibration tooling or eval hooks?
[04:25] Eli Chen: We have Redwood Optimize tooling — you can run prompt/eval suites, monitor regressions, and set quality alerts tied to prompts. Also retriever/LLM function-calling helps by constraining outputs to function signatures.
[04:39] Sofia Ruiz: What's the recommended approach for 20k+ notes? Chunk + RAG, or native 64k context?
[04:46] Maya Kapoor: If you need global cross-references across a 20k note, 64k native context avoids chunk alignment issues but is heavier. We often suggest a hybrid: chunking with overlap for extraction plus selective full-context runs for summarization. We'll prototype both.
[05:00] Eli Chen: Also, cost-wise 64k contexts are more expensive per call. Redwood Optimize can show unit economics and suggest quantization and caching to reduce cost.
[05:11] Dr. Arjun Patel: Any red flags on HIPAA? We need a BA agreement; is Redwood open to an exec BA?
[05:18] Eli Chen: Yes, we have customers under BAAs; for Private deployments it's straightforward. We'll surface legal contacts and the required compliance artifacts.
[05:26] Sofia Ruiz: Could you also include notes on model updates/rollouts? We need stable pinned versions for audits.
[05:32] Maya Kapoor: You can pin model versions and rollouts; we support canary and automatic fallback to compatible variants if a model regresses. We keep prior versions for reproducibility.
[05:44] Liam O'Connor: On observability, can we get token-level cost and per-request latency?
[05:50] Eli Chen: Yes Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces, and error analysis. We'll include screenshots in the follow-up pack.
[05:59] Speaker 2: (background)
[06:04] Sofia Ruiz: For benchmarks, we want: multilingual extraction (en/es/pt/zh), structured JSON output accuracy, latency p95 for short vs long, and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:15] Eli Chen: Perfect, that's what we'll run. We'll propose a benchmark plan in the follow-up.
[06:20] Dr. Arjun Patel: A practical question — do you support on-prem air-gapped? We have a pilot site that will be offline for months.
[06:28] Maya Kapoor: We do: Private on-prem package with a control plane option; for air-gapped we ship an appliance and we integrate with local KMS/HSM. That is a deeper engagement with our Enterprise team.
[06:40] Sofia Ruiz: Who else from Redwood should we loop in for legal/procurement?
[06:44] Eli Chen: I'll include our solutions and legal reps. Also our SRE onboarding lead for networking.
[06:50] Dr. Arjun Patel: Timeline — we're targeting a pilot in 6 weeks and production in Q4.
[06:56] Eli Chen: That sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get benchmarks done in 2 weeks so you can decide sizing.
[07:02] Maya Kapoor: Quick note on function calling — we'll include code snippets showing how a model calls your retrieval API then returns a function-structured JSON.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: Great. Also, do you provide per-tenant isolation metrics for Dedicated? We need to ensure noisy neighbor won't impact latency.
[07:17] Eli Chen: Dedicated runs on reserved pools; we have isolation guarantees and autoscaling policies to avoid neighbor issues. We'll share SLA language.
[07:27] Sofia Ruiz: Any comments on model license for open models? We need clarity on redistribution if we go Private with a licensed variant.
[07:35] Maya Kapoor: License compliance varies; we can help with the legal considerations and preferred model lists. For some models a redistribution or special licensing is required.
[07:44] Speaker 1: (phone glitch)
[07:48] Eli Chen: Ok, recap quick: action items — share bench spreadsheet, SOC2 and security pack, propose dedicated sizing, Sofia share eval dataset, Liam confirm VPC constraints. Agreed to schedule technical deep-dive for benchmarks.
[08:04] Dr. Arjun Patel: Sounds good. One last question — will streaming be available for long summaries to start sending partial results?
[08:12] Maya Kapoor: Yes, we support streaming tokens and chunked structured streaming so you can start processing partial outputs.
[08:19] Sofia Ruiz: Thanks, everyone. We'll get the dataset and network constraints over by Wednesday.
[08:24] Eli Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the pack and proposed schedule.
[08:29] (meeting ends)
notes: Follow-up to include benchmark plan, performance spreadsheet, security artifacts, and proposed Dedicated sizing. Customer to provide eval data and network constraints.
